manifest.name: Point of Sale UBL
manifest.summary: UBL in the Point of Sale
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

security.note: No own security artefacts (0 ACLs, 0 record rules, 0 groups): the model is an AbstractModel with no table, called in sudo/server context by consumer localisation modules.

views.note: No views and no XML data files (xml_loc=0): the module is a headless XML-builder library; any UI (download/submit buttons) is added by the consuming localisation (e.g. l10n_jo_edi_pos).

behavioral_notes.observation: The single public entry point. It mirrors account.edi.xml.ubl_20._export_invoice but for a pos.order instead of an account.move: it sets vals['pos_order'] re-contextualised to the customer's lang (pos_order.with_context(lang=pos_order.partner_id.lang)), builds the structured document_node via _get_pos_order_node, evaluates _export_pos_order_constraints into an errors set, picks an Invoice/CreditNote template + cac/cbc/ext nsmap via the inherited _get_document_template / _get_document_nsmap, renders the tree with odoo.addons.account.tools.dict_to_xml, and returns a (xml_bytes, errors_set) tuple. So like its account.move sibling a structurally-invalid order is reported in the second tuple element rather than silently shipped. None of this generation pipeline is visible in field metadata (the model has 0 fields, 27 methods).

This is where the POS->UBL mapping diverges from the invoice builder. _add_pos_order_config_vals fixes the EDI parties and journal directly from the order rather than from an account.move: document_type = 'invoice' if pos_order.amount_total >= 0 else 'credit_note'; supplier = pos_order.company_id.partner_id.commercial_partner_id; customer = pos_order.partner_id; journal = pos_order.config_id.invoice_journal_id; currency_id = pos_order.currency_id; and the flags use_company_currency=False, fixed_taxes_as_allowance_charges=True. _add_pos_order_base_lines_vals derives the tax base lines straight from the order via pos_order._prepare_tax_base_line_values(), then calls account.tax._add_tax_details_in_base_lines and _round_base_lines_tax_details so the same EN16931 tax-detail machinery the invoice path uses is reused on raw POS lines. This cross-model adaptation (account.move semantics expressed over a pos.order) is pure Python.

Two POS-specific deviations from a normal invoice document. (1) After delegating to the inherited _add_document_monetary_total_nodes, the builder injects cbc:PrepaidAmount = tax_exclusive_amount - pos_order.amount_paid and cbc:PayableAmount = pos_order.amount_paid into the LegalMonetaryTotal node, encoding that a POS sale is already (fully or partly) tendered at the till, unlike a billed-then-paid invoice. (2) _export_pos_order_constraints returns {} -- an empty, intentionally overridable hook: the base POS-UBL builder enforces no business rules itself, leaving country-specific EN16931/clearance constraints (and any AccountingSupplierParty/tax-id requirements) to the localisation subclass. Line items are built one document_node per non-allowance base line via _add_pos_order_line_nodes (allowance/charge lines are emitted as AllowanceCharges, not InvoiceLines), and the item Name/Description falls back to the POS line.name. These value- and constraint-level decisions are not reverse-engineerable from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: consumer wiring: module defines the builder but never calls it; l10n_jo_edi_pos is the only consumer
behavioral_notes.observation: pos_edi_ubl is a reusable library with no caller of its own -- _export_pos_order is invoked nowhere inside this module (it adds no pos.order extension, no attachment field, no invoice hook). The sole consumer in the codebase is the Jordan localisation l10n_jo_edi_pos (depends ['l10n_jo_edi','pos_edi_ubl']), which subclasses _name='pos.edi.xml.ubl_21.jo' (_inherit pos.edi.xml.ubl_21), and from pos.order._submit_to_jofotara / _compute_l10n_jo_edi_pos_computed_xml calls env['pos.edi.xml.ubl_21.jo']._export_pos_order(order)[0], base64-encodes the bytes, POSTs them to the JoFotara clearance API, and stores the returned XML + EINV_QR as an ir.attachment on the pos.order. So the POS-order->UBL XML attachment and any invoice/e-invoice hooking happen in the localisation, not here; pos_edi_ubl only supplies the format-neutral UBL 2.1 scaffolding that a fiscal localisation specialises. This 'engine vs caller' split is exactly the kind of fact metadata cannot show.

frontend_gap3.present = false: 0 JS files, 0 XML templates, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches, no asset bundles. The module ships only models/pos_edi_ubl_21.py (220 py LOC) and __manifest__/__init__; it is a server-side serialisation library with no client-side footprint and no XML data files. integrations_gap7 is empty (no outbound HTTP / SDK / api-keys) -- the actual network call to a tax authority lives in the consuming localisation (l10n_jo_edi_pos -> JoFotara), not in pos_edi_ubl.

it_architecture.application: pos_edi_ubl (headless UBL 2.1 e-invoice builder for Point of Sale orders; an abstract serialisation library extending account_edi_ubl_cii's account.edi.xml.ubl_21 onto pos.order)
logical_data_erm: pos.edi.xml.ubl_21._export_pos_order(pos_order) consumes pos.order (+ pos.order.line base lines, pos.config.invoice_journal_id, res.partner supplier/customer, res.currency, account.tax details)
information_flows: depends: point_of_sale (provides pos.order / pos.config / _prepare_tax_base_line_values), account_edi_ubl_cii (provides account.edi.xml.ubl_21 + the _add_document_* / _get_document_* node builders and dict_to_xml rendering)

build: pos.order -> _export_pos_order -> document_node dict (header, AccountingSupplierParty=company commercial partner, AccountingCustomerParty=order partner, AllowanceCharge, TaxTotal, LegalMonetaryTotal with Prepaid/PayableAmount, InvoiceLine/CreditNoteLine per product line) -> dict_to_xml -> (UBL 2.1 XML bytes, errors set)
no own side-effect: this module attaches nothing and posts nowhere; the (xml_bytes, errors) tuple is returned to a caller
consumer side-effect (l10n_jo_edi_pos): pos.edi.xml.ubl_21.jo._export_pos_order(order) -> base64 -> POST JoFotara -> ir.attachment(res_model='pos.order') + l10n_jo_edi_pos_qr stored on the order

capabilities: Serialise a POS Order to a UBL 2.1 e-invoice / credit-note document (format scaffolding)
Reuse Accounting's EN16931 tax-detail / monetary-total machinery over raw POS order lines
Encode POS tendering in the e-document (PrepaidAmount / PayableAmount from amount_paid)
Provide an overridable constraints + node-builder framework for country POS e-invoicing localisations
value_streams: Provide-POS-UBL-Builder: a fiscal localisation subclasses pos.edi.xml.ubl_21 -> calls _export_pos_order(pos_order) -> gets a validated UBL 2.1 XML (+ errors) it then clears/attaches to the order (no end-to-end flow within this module itself)
information_concepts: account.edi.xml.ubl_21 (parent invoice UBL builder being specialised)
policies: auto_install=false: unlike account_edi_ubl_cii (auto-installs with account), this POS-UBL library is opt-in -- pulled in only by a localisation that needs POS e-invoicing
document_type is invoice for amount_total>=0 else credit_note (sign-driven, no separate refund object)
_export_pos_order_constraints returns {} by design: the base builder imposes no business rules; compliance constraints are the localisation's responsibility
product lines become InvoiceLines/CreditNoteLines; non-product (allowance/charge) lines become AllowanceCharges, not lines
stakeholders: Fiscal localisation developer (subclasses the builder for a national POS e-invoicing mandate)
Accountant / Tax authority (ultimate consumer of the cleared e-invoice produced by the localisation)
POS Cashier (rings the pos.order that becomes the source document, indirectly)

classification.rationale: pos_edi_ubl is a support / compliance scaffold, not a sell-flow bridge -- it is deliberately classified like its parent account_edi_ubl_cii (support / 9.0) rather than like the other POS bridges (chain / 3.0). Reasoning from the code: (1) It owns a single AbstractModel with no table, no fields, no routes, no UI, no security and no data files -- it produces no sale, payment, delivery or order state; it only serialises an already-rung pos.order into a legally-structured UBL 2.1 XML document. That is infrastructure for fiscal/e-invoicing compliance, the Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support' pattern (an enabler of the firm's invoicing back-office), not a value chain that converts inputs to a sold output. (2) Its centre of gravity is the EN16931/UBL document model: it reuses account_edi_ubl_cii's _add_document_* tax-detail and LegalMonetaryTotal builders and emits AccountingSupplierParty/TaxTotal/PayableAmount -- pure financial-document machinery, which maps to APQC 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (specifically the 9.x receivables / e-invoice document-exchange family), exactly where account_edi_ubl_cii sits. (3) Decisively, the module performs no selling and is not even invoked in the sell flow: _export_pos_order has no caller inside this module; it is a library specialised by country localisations (only l10n_jo_edi_pos in the tree) that handle the actual fiscal submission. So while the SOURCE document originates from a retail sale (giving it a faint chain flavour, and justifying why one might argue 3.0), the module's own activity is compliance serialisation -- support, not primary. Chain/3.0 was therefore rejected: pos_edi_ubl adds zero primary-chain value and would never appear in a Market-and-Sell value stream except as the downstream regulatory artefact, which is precisely the 9.0/support concern its parent already owns.

standard_capabilities: produce a UBL 2.1 Invoice/CreditNote document_node from a pos.order (header, supplier/customer party, allowance-charges, tax totals, line items)
reuse Accounting's EN16931 tax-detail and monetary-total computation (account.tax._add_tax_details_in_base_lines / _round_base_lines_tax_details) over POS base lines
encode already-tendered POS amounts as cbc:PrepaidAmount / cbc:PayableAmount
return a (xml_bytes, errors) tuple so validation failures are surfaced, not silently shipped
offer an empty, overridable _export_pos_order_constraints + per-node hooks for localisation-specific business rules
typical_fits: a country POS e-invoicing localisation that needs UBL 2.1 output for till receipts/orders (e.g. l10n_jo_edi_pos / JoFotara)
extending POS e-invoicing to a clearance regime by subclassing pos.edi.xml.ubl_21 and overriding the party/header/constraint hooks
generating a structured e-document for a pos.order without first creating an account.move
common_gaps: no end-to-end flow on its own: it neither attaches the XML to the order nor transmits it -- a localisation must call _export_pos_order and persist/submit the result
no business-rule enforcement by default (_export_pos_order_constraints is empty) -- each mandate must supply its own EN16931/clearance checks
not auto-installed and not POS-UI wired: no download/send button, no pos.order field -- the consumer adds those
no CII / Factur-X path here (UBL 2.1 only); CII output would reuse account.edi.xml.cii via a different builder
PrepaidAmount/PayableAmount assume the till tendering model; partial-payment or deferred-settlement POS scenarios may need localisation overrides
drive_hints: odoo shell: order = env['pos.order'].search([('state','in',('paid','done','invoiced'))], limit=1); xml, errs = env['pos.edi.xml.ubl_21']._export_pos_order(order); print(errs); print(xml[:600])
odoo shell: env['pos.edi.xml.ubl_21']._fields and not env['pos.edi.xml.ubl_21']._table  # AbstractModel: no rows, only methods (27)
odoo shell (with l10n_jo_edi_pos installed): env['pos.edi.xml.ubl_21.jo']._export_pos_order(order)[0][:400]  # the only concrete consumer
grep: rg -n '_export_pos_order' addons --glob '!addons/pos_edi_ubl/**'  # shows l10n_jo_edi_pos is the sole caller

open_questions: Whether any official Odoo module other than l10n_jo_edi_pos (or third-party localisations) consumes pos.edi.xml.ubl_21, and whether a generic 'attach UBL to pos.order' path is intended upstream.
Exact tax-category / exemption-reason coverage when POS lines carry taxes not classified for UBL (the base builder inherits account.tax mappings but adds no POS-specific ones).
How _export_pos_order behaves for a pure refund (amount_total<0 credit_note) versus a mixed-sign order, and whether PrepaidAmount stays consistent.
Whether the UBLVersionID '2.0' emitted in the header (vs the model's '2.1' naming) is intentional for downstream validators.
